events.title: Salem Witch Trials Begin with First Examinations
events.description: Magistrates John Hathorne and Jonathan Corwin began examining Sarah Good, Sarah Osborne, and Tituba in Salem Village, Massachusetts Bay Colony, after accusations of witchcraft by local girls.
events.significance: These examinations launched one of the most infamous episodes of mass hysteria in American history, resulting in the execution of 20 people and serving as a lasting cautionary tale about due process, religious extremism, and scapegoating.

events.title: Articles of Confederation Ratified
events.description: Maryland's ratification on this date completed approval by all 13 states, and the Articles of Confederation took effect, establishing the first governing framework of the United States.
events.significance: The Articles created the first national government of the United States, and their weaknesses led directly to the Constitutional Convention of 1787 and the creation of the current U.S. Constitution.

events.title: Yellowstone Becomes the First U.S. National Park
events.description: President Ulysses S. Grant signed the Yellowstone National Park Protection Act, setting aside land in Wyoming and Montana territories as a public park.
events.significance: Yellowstone is widely considered the first national park in the world, inspiring the global national park movement and modern conservation of natural landscapes.

events.title: Castle Bravo Hydrogen Bomb Test
events.description: The United States detonated the Castle Bravo thermonuclear device at Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands. Its yield of about 15 megatons was more than double predictions and spread radioactive fallout over inhabited islands and a Japanese fishing vessel.
events.significance: It was the largest nuclear weapon ever tested by the U.S. and caused a serious radiological disaster, fueling international concern over nuclear testing and contributing to later test-ban efforts.

events.title: Peace Corps Established
events.description: President John F. Kennedy signed an executive order creating the Peace Corps, a volunteer program sending Americans to developing countries to assist with education, health, and development.
events.significance: The Peace Corps became a lasting symbol of American soft power and international service, with hundreds of thousands of volunteers serving in more than 140 countries.
